reasons.A: Best catches the passage's ironic first-person stance: disarming disclaimers ('I do not propose...', the parenthetical 'I merely record it'), concessions followed by a turn, short blunt sentences ('Nobody disputes it.') among long semicolon-joined periods, and double dashes used as the author uses them.
reasons.B: Right period diction and dry understatement ('a little quaint', 'Granted;') with semicolons and dashes, but it argues more flatly and explains more, with less of the author's teasing self-positioning towards the reader.
reasons.C: Smooth and modern-earnest. Balanced lists and anaphora ('Departments multiply, journals multiply') and a lyrical definition of culture replace the author's irony. There are no double dashes and few semicolons, so it reads as a different writer.
